summary: Throughput degradation in reserved pool due to heartbeat compression & GPU reservation fragmentation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ShiftLane reports sustained p50/p99 throughput degradation in their dedicated GPU pool starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. Traffic pattern: many short-lived chat streams with intermittent short bursts (~3–7s) from thousands of devices. Impact: customer facing application experienced 30–45% throughput loss and increased queueing across several routes pinned to redwood-open-7b.

Impact:
- Throughput p50 dropped by ~38% compared to baseline for the dedicated pool supporting ShiftLane.
- P99 latency increased and request queue lengths grew, triggering fallback to a lower-tier pool for some requests.
- Customer reports degraded user experience and increased error surface where fallback capacity hit rate grew to ~12%.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved capacity (customer tier: dedicated) in us-east region.
- Serving runtime version: 3.12.1.
- Allocator daemon version: allocator-1.7.0.
- Autoscaler policy: predictive-with-warmup (default warmup 60s).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Synthetic short-chat flood from 10k simulated clients with keep-alive streams of 3–10s each.
2) Observe allocator logs and GPU slot attachments during burst windows (09:10–10:00 UTC).
3) Note that many slots remain reserved but unused for short periods; subsequent microbursts fail to consolidate into large batches.

Observed signals & logs (snippets):
- Allocator: "heartbeat: compressed interval 190ms -> drop 0.6, reservation_split_detected=TRUE" repeated.
- Scheduler: increased slot fragmentation metric (slot_free_frag=0.42 -> 0.68) during window.
- Autoscaler: did not scale up promptly because free_reservation_count was >0 but fragmented and not usable for incoming microbatches.
- Metric: kv_cache_hit stable, but batch_sizes dropped from baseline 16->7 on average.

Initial hypothesis:
- Heartbeat compression optimization in allocator combined with noisy, short-lived streams causes frequent reservation splits (fragmentation) across GPUs. The allocator marks many small slice reservations as "reserved" (to avoid thrashing) but the compressed heartbeat makes them appear healthy and prevents proactive compaction/reclaim for immediate consolidation. Result: available but fragmented capacity cannot form useful batches, leading to throughput collapse.

Requested next steps:
- Confirm with SRE whether heartbeat compression thresholds changed in allocator-1.7.0.
- Run controlled repro with heartbeat compression disabled in a staging pool.
- Apply emergency mitigation (force compaction / expire small reservations earlier) in prod for affected pool if safe.

Additional notes:
- Customer provided trace IDs and a short heap of logs (attached in ticket).
- This appears different from classic noisy-tenant preemption; here slots are reserved (not preempted) and are prevented from compaction by compressed health signals.

investigation_notes: Allocator config diff: heartbeat_compression.enabled=true in 1.7.0; compression_window_ms lowered from 200->120 in last deploy (2026-03-01). This made heartbeats appear smoother but reduced visibility into transient reservation liveness.

Repro in staging with high short-stream fanout: when compression enabled, reservation_split events increase 3x and compaction loop runs less frequently because compressed heartbeats bypass compaction triggers.
Telemetry: free_reservation_count stayed >0 but usable_contiguous_slots metric declined sharply, indicating fragmentation rather than true scarcity.

Autoscaler logic relies on free_reservation_count for scale decisions; because reservations existed (fragmented), autoscaler refrained from scaling up even though effective batchable capacity was low.
Mitigation implemented: lowered short-reservation TTL and triggered immediate compaction job. This reclaimed fragmented slices and allowed batch formation. Patch ID: allocator-hotfix-6123.
Risk assessment: disabling heartbeat compression broadly could increase allocator churn; scoped change preferred (per-pool override).
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: applied per-pool override to reduce short-reservation TTL (45s -> 12s) and forced compaction. Result: throughput recovered ~22% immediately and batch_sizes climbed from 7->11 average.

Planned follow-up (owner: allocator team):
- Roll a per-pool heartbeat_compression.threshold config and default to less aggressive compression for dedicated pools with many short-lived streams (ETA: 2026-03-21).
- Update autoscaler heuristics to consider contiguous_batchable_slots instead of raw free_reservation_count (design doc created, PR planned).
- Add runbook entry for "heartbeat-compression-induced-fragmentation" including monitoring playbook and safe rollback steps.

Customer communication: Notified customer of temporary mitigation and ongoing work; scheduled post-incident review and delivery plan for permanent change.
